readmeExcerpt:
# Summarize 📝 — Link in, signal out.






Summarize extracts clean text and produces summaries from web pages, files, YouTube videos, podcasts, and other audio or video. Use it from the Node.js CLI or from the Chrome Side Panel and Firefox Sidebar.



```console
$ summarize "https://example.com" --extract --plain
This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission. Avoid use in operations.
[Learn more](https://iana.org/domains/example)
```

## Install

Run it once without installing:

```bash
npx -y @steipete/summarize --version
```

Or install the CLI with npm or Homebrew:

```bash
npm install --global @steipete/summarize
```

```bash
brew install summarize
```

The npm package requires Node.js 24 or newer. Homebrew/core and the [macOS archives on GitHub Releases](https://github.com/steipete/summarize/releases/latest) provide standalone builds. See the [installation guide](docs/install.md) for optional media tools and platform notes.

## Quick start

Extract readable content without an API key:

```bash
summarize "https://example.com" --extract --plain
```

For a model-generated summary, configure a [supported provider](docs/llm.md) or use an authenticated coding CLI:

```bash
summarize "https://example.com" --cli codex
```

The default `auto` model chooses among configured providers. The [five-minute quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) covers API keys, local models, files, YouTube, podcasts, and JSON output.

### Languages

The CLI and Chrome/Firefox extension interfaces support English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, and Turkish.

The interface follows your system or browser language, with English as the fallback. Use `--locale de` or `SUMMARIZE_LOCALE=de` for German CLI help and progress, or select **Interface language** in the extension’s options. Summary language stays independent:

```bash
summarize "https://example.com" --locale de --language japanese
```

The [localization guide](docs/localization.md) covers locale selection, translation glossaries, adding languages, and the CI checks that keep catalogs complete.

## What it handles

| Input                        | Processing path                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Web pages                    | Readability extraction, with optional Markdown and Firecrawl fallbacks |
| PDFs, images, and text files | File-aware extraction and model attachments where supported            |
| YouTube and podcasts         | Published transcripts first, then configured transcription fallbacks   |
| Audio and video              | Local or cloud transcription, with optional speaker labels             |
| Video slides                 | Scene-based frames, optional OCR, and timestamped output               |

Use `--extract` when you only need clean content, `--json` for a stable automation envelope, and `--slides` for video frames. The [command reference](docs/commands/index.md) documents every flag.



## Browser extension

Install [Summarize Side Panel from the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/summarize/cejgnmmhbbpdmjnfppjdfkocebngehfg) to summarize the active tab, chat with its content, and work with video transcripts and slides.

Direct mode runs without a companion service. Browser media uses Chrome capabilities for local transcription and slide extraction; the optional daemon adds CLI model backends, native media tools, OCR, shared caches, and Firefox media support.

To pair the installed CLI, copy the token shown by the extension and run:

```bash
summarize daemon install --token <TOKEN>
```

See the [extension setup](apps/chrome-extension/README.md) and [architecture and troubleshooting guide](docs/chrome-extension.md).

## Media and slides

Summarize prefers existing captions and podcast transcripts before it transcribes media. Native `ffmpeg`, `yt-dlp`, and `tesseract` extend codec, YouTube slide, and OCR support; a bundled WebAssembly FFmpeg path covers common media without a native install.



The focused guides describe [YouTube extraction](docs/youtube.md), [media routing](docs/media.md), [slides](docs/slides.md), and [local ONNX transcription](docs/nvidia-onnx-transcription.md).

## Models and configuration

Model IDs use `provider/model` names. Summarize works with configured API providers, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, OpenRouter free models, and authenticated coding CLIs such as Codex, Claude, Gemini, OpenClaw, GitHub Copilot, and Grok.

Configuration lives at `~/.summarize/config.json`; command-line flags take precedence. Inspect the effective setup without exposing keys:

```bash
summarize status
```

Read the [model guide](docs/llm.md), [automatic selection rules](docs/model-auto.md), [CLI provider guide](docs/cli.md), and [configuration reference](docs/config.md) for the full setup.

## Library

For programmatic extraction without the CLI dependency surface, install [`@steipete/summarize-core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@steipete/summarize-core):

```bash
npm install @steipete/summarize-core
```

The package exports focused content and prompt entry points. See the [core package README](packages/core/README.md) for usage.

## Documentation

Start with the [documentation index](docs/README.md), then follow the guide for your task:

- [Installation](docs/install.md) and [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md)
- [Commands](docs/commands/index.md) and [configuration](docs/config.md)
- [Website extraction](docs/website.md) and [Firecrawl fallback](docs/firecrawl.md)
- [YouTube](docs/youtube.md), [media](docs/media.md), and [slides](docs/slides.md)
- [Agent skill](.agents/skills/summarize/SKILL.md) for automated workflows

## Development

Requires Node.js 24 and the workspace's pinned pnpm version through Corepack.

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
pnpm check
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for repository layout and extension workflows.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

releases.name: v0.26.0
releases.body:
**Highlights:** complete browser chat context, reliable whisper.cpp transcription and direct media downloads, Antigravity model selection, and security fixes for node-forge, Undici, and HTML/Markdown processing.

- Browser chat: keep media previews separate from full source content so the first question includes the whole article, preserving transcript provenance and navigation safety (#553, thanks @vincent-peng).
- Transcription: pass configured environment variables and PATH to whisper.cpp discovery and transcription processes (#554, thanks @vincent-peng).
- Media: accept direct MP4 downloads with unknown codec metadata while continuing to reject known video-only formats (#549, fixes #548, thanks @zewelor).
- Transcription: keep whisper.cpp timestamp decoding enabled to preserve speech at 30-second window boundaries while retaining plain-text output (#543, thanks @vlauciani).
- Browser chat: reuse existing summaries for follow-up questions and history, honor Browser media mode during context extraction, and return context errors promptly to the pending chat request (#537, thanks @laolxun).
- Antigravity: honor `cli.agy.model` (previously ignored) and support `cli/agy/<model>`; r

releases.name: v0.25.3
releases.body:
**Highlights:** security fixes for Markdown rendering and Vite, plus more reliable OpenRouter reasoning, media extraction, and transcription uploads.

- Security: backport Markdown rendering denial-of-service fixes and update Vite editor-launch protection while retaining the seven-day dependency stabilization policy.
- OpenRouter: forward reasoning effort and omit implicit output limits for text completions and streams; retain provider error diagnostics (#527, fixes #519, thanks @Ehsan-hash).
- Media and CLI: terminate timed-out process trees, handle early child stdin closure, and close slide image streams on disconnect without masking extraction failures during cleanup (#520, #521, #524, thanks @SebTardif).
- Transcription: abort stalled FAL and AssemblyAI uploads and response bodies while preserving the existing post-upload processing allowance (#522, thanks @SebTardif).
- Browser extraction: bound YouTube audio downloads without a content length and honor the configured summarize fetch timeout, with a two-minute fallback (#523, #526, thanks @SebTardif).
- Spotify: reject lookalike hostnames when resolving episode IDs (#525, thanks @SebTardif).
- Maintenance: refresh stabilized

aiSummary.oneLiner: A fast, media-aware summarization tool available as a CLI, Chrome Side Panel, and Firefox Sidebar.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Summarize is a versatile tool designed to provide rapid, clean summaries of URLs, local files, and various media types directly within your existing workflow. It intelligently routes processing based on the input type, automatically extracting web readability data, fetching existing YouTube transcripts, or utilizing local ONNX transcription for raw audio. Beyond simple text generation, it can produce rich 'video slides' by extracting timestamped scene frames, applying OCR, and combining them with transcript data. The tool leverages multiple LLM backends, including local models and commercial APIs, and integrates seamlessly into browser sidebars or terminal scripts.
keyFeatures: Media awareness: Automatically detects input types and routes them through optimized processing paths, prioritizing existing transcripts before transcribing audio.
Video slide generation: Extracts scene-based frames from videos, applies optional OCR, and pairs them with timestamps for rich visual summaries.
Browser integration: Operates directly within a Chrome Side Panel or Firefox Sidebar, maintaining chat history and streaming AI responses incrementally.
Broad model support: Works with configured API providers, local Ollama models, and authenticated coding CLIs like Codex or Claude.
CLI extraction mode: Provides a pure extraction mode (`--extract`) to pull clean text or JSON envelopes for scripted automation workflows.
Local transcription fallback: Utilizes bundled WebAssembly FFmpeg or local ONNX transcription for processing media without cloud dependencies.

useCases.title: Rapid Content Consumption
useCases.description: Users quickly grasp the key points of long articles or YouTube videos directly from their browser sidebar without watching the entire content.

useCases.title: Visual Video Notetaking
useCases.description: Researchers use the CLI to generate timestamped video slides with OCR data from educational lectures to capture whiteboard diagrams.

useCases.title: CLI Workflow Automation
useCases.description: Developers integrate the tool into terminal scripts using the JSON output flag to automatically summarize daily log files or RSS feeds.

useCases.title: Offline Media Transcription
useCases.description: Journalists use the local ONNX transcription capabilities to securely process and summarize sensitive audio interviews without sending data to the cloud.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Researchers, developers, and power users who need to quickly process large amounts of information from various sources, requiring a flexible tool that works across browsers and the terminal. Familiarity with Node.js is recommended.
